title: Quotient transitions under normalized integral coefficient comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite and X any scheme, with integral encoding A [def-pe-integral-presentation-encoding], finite encodings e_n [def-pe-finite-discrete-presentation-encoding], and identity-on-abelian-sections ordinary restriction squares a_n. Let b_n be finite derived comparison isomorphisms between A.derived followed by completed scalar extension and the internal derived reduction followed by e_n.ordinaryDerived [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Assume their restricted comparisons c_n carry the specified completed tensor units to the images under A.derived of the internal derived adjunction units. Then sfDerivedReductionTransition_n followed by c_n equals c_(n+1) followed by A.derived of integralStep_n. The transitions and units are exactly those of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. The statement asserts only this transition equation, for arbitrary derived K, including unbounded and zero complexes. The prime, coefficient extension and small site use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; module sheaves and their derived categories use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: The inverse mate of each localized restriction square is an isomorphism because the horizontal functors are equivalences. Injectivity of the derived tensor/restriction Hom bijection shows that the unit equation uniquely fixes its components. Hence the supplied b_n is this normalized inverse mate.

Take an internal K-flat representative. The section reconstruction and relabelling along a ring isomorphism preserve K-flatness: apply the tensor comparison to every acyclic test complex and its image under the inverse equivalence. The normalized restriction square makes the balancing relation on the two finite tensor constructions identical, so the localized inverse mate is the comparison sending s tensor x to s tensor x.

The consecutive quotient chain map on both representatives sends s tensor x to rho(s) tensor x. This is finite-linear since the quotient projections compose. Its transpose is the smaller tensor unit, since rho(1)=1. The defining internal scalar adjunction, its canonical compositor, and the representative characterization of sfDerivedReductionTransition identify these chain maps with precisely the displayed transitions. Tensor generation and sheafification give equality before localization. Counit invertibility on K-flat representatives and naturality transport the equality to every derived K. The calculation also applies at n=0 and on the empty site.

theorem integral_completion_transition_comparison (A : Encoding l E X) :
    letI := (Padic.coefficientExtensionAbsoluteValue l E).toNormedField
    ∀ (e : ∀ n : ℕ,
      FiniteDiscreteOrdinary.Encoding (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) X)
      (a : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Mod.comap (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n) ⋙ A.modules.functor ≅
        (e n).ordinary.functor ⋙ scalarReductionRestriction.{u, u} l E X n),
    let r (n : ℕ) :
        AdicCompletion.restrict l E X n ⋙ A.derived.functor ≅
          (e n).ordinaryDerived.functor ⋙ scalarReductionDerivedRestriction.{u, u} l E X n :=
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard
        (FiniteDiscreteOrdinary.Ordinary (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)) X)
      letI := scalarReductionRestrictionLimits.{u, u} l E X n
      letI := scalarReductionRestrictionColimits.{u, u} l E X n
      (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
        (Mod.comap (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)) A.modules.functor).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso (a n) ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso (e n).ordinary.functor
          (scalarReductionRestriction.{u, u} l E X n)
    let c (b : ∀ n : ℕ,
      A.derived.functor ⋙ scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E X n ≅
        AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n ⋙ (e n).ordinaryDerived.functor)
        (n : ℕ) (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)) :
        (sfDerivedReductionRestricted l E X n).obj (A.derived.functor.obj K) ≅
          A.derived.functor.obj (AdicCompletion.integralLevel l E X K n) :=
      (scalarReductionDerivedRestriction.{u, u} l E X n).mapIso ((b n).app K) ≪≫
        ((r n).app ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n).obj K)).symm
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
        (AdicCompletion.finiteRing l E X n)),
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X)).map
          ((a n).hom.app M) =
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf
          (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X)).map
            (eqToIso (congrArg (fun F ↦ F.obj
              ((Mod.comap (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)).obj M)) A.functor_eq)).hom ≫
          (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (integralCoefficientSheaf.{u, u} l E X n)).map
            (eqToIso (congrArg (fun F ↦ F.obj M) (e n).ordinary_functor)).inv) →
    ∀ (b : ∀ n : ℕ,
      A.derived.functor ⋙ scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E X n ≅
        AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n ⋙ (e n).ordinaryDerived.functor),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)),
        (sfDerivedReductionUnit l E X n).app (A.derived.functor.obj K) ≫
          (c b n K).hom = A.derived.functor.map
            ((Mod.derivedExtendMapDerivedCategoryAdjunction
              (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)).unit.app K)) →
      ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X)) (n : ℕ),
        (sfDerivedReductionTransition l E X n).app (A.derived.functor.obj K) ≫
            (c b n K).hom = (c b (n + 1) K).hom ≫
          A.derived.functor.map (AdicCompletion.integralStep l E X K n)
